Sara — thanks for the clear asks and for the redlines. Looping in Laura (account lead) and Karthik (sales ops/contracts) to scope and confirm.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- Uptime: we can discuss 99.95% for hosted and 99.99% for Dedicated but need to align on measurement windows (monthly vs rolling 30d) and the exact definition of outage (service-level vs per-route).
- Latency: the P95 numbers depend heavily on model family, request size, and region. For most Redwood-curated models we can hit ~150–200ms P95 on hosted for short sequences (<=128 tokens) in us-east. Dedicated pools have predictable queuing, so the 80ms P95 target is plausible for optimized model configurations but will require pinning model quantization and concurrency limits in the order form.
- Credits: Redwood typically uses a sliding credit scale tied to monthly availability; we'll circulate our standard credit table and suggest a one-way SLA exception carveout for planned maintenance and for agreed experimental features.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik takes the redlines, drafts alternate order form language for 'Dedicated capacity' (including quantization/profile locking and concurrency ceilings).
2) Laura and I review latency SLIs with our Applied ML team to produce model-specific targets and an appendix to the SLA.
3) Redwood Contracts will propose final wording for maintenance windows and credit calculation.

Would you be available for a 30-min call on Wednesday 14th at noon ET? If not, suggest a time.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Sara — appreciate the detailed spreadsheet. I've pulled in our Applied ML lead and Contracts to make sure we have defensible numbers. A few clarifications before the call:

- Can you confirm expected traffic profile (qps, average tokens per request, peak concurrency)? That will materially change achievable P95.
- Is Greenfield intending to route all production traffic through hosted endpoints, or do you expect hybrid (hosted + private Dedicated pools)? The order form language differs for Dedicated because we can commit to more aggressive latency SLOs when capacity is reserved.

In terms of order form language we typically include:
- A 'Model Profile' appendix listing the model family, quantization, and concurrency cap that the latency SLO applies to.
- 'Capacity Reservation' clause: the customer pays for a committed GPU pool size; Redwood will provision and maintain the pool and commit to throughput SLOs up to the reserved capacity. Burst capacity and autoscaling are explicitly out of scope of the latency SLA unless otherwise agreed.

I've attached a draft snippet for the order form (GF_OrderForm_Scopes_v1.docx) outlining the Model Profile appendix and concurrency caps — think of it as our starting point for negotiation. For maintenance windows, we generally commit to <=4 hours/month for non-emergency maintenance and 72-hour notice; emergency maintenance can be invoked with as-short-as-24-hour notice, and we provide a post-incident report within 3 business days.

I'll be on the call tomorrow with Karthik and Dylan; looking forward to working through the specifics.

Cheers,

Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sara / team — thanks for the productive call yesterday. Per our action items, attaching the initial proposed credit matrix and suggested redline language below. Please treat this as our starting proposal and we'll refine after your legal reviews.

Key proposal highlights:
- Uptime measurement: rolling 30-day window, per-customer service availability (ingestion + generation endpoints).
- Proposed availability SLOs: Hosted API 99.95% (monthly), Dedicated 99.995% (monthly) — note Dedicated number is higher because reserved pools exclude multi-tenant scheduling overhead.
- Latency SLOs: we propose a model-profiled approach. Example entry: 'gpt-medium-quant8' — P95 <= 120ms for Dedicated with concurrency cap of 64; Hosted regional endpoints — P95 <= 220ms for sequences <=256 tokens. We'll export model-profile SLIs as an appendix.
- Credits: 5% service credit for monthly availability between 99.0% - 99.95%; 10% credit for <99.0%; caps at 50% monthly credit. Credits are applied to invoice for the following billing cycle.
- Maintenance carveouts: Planned maintenance (up to 4 hours/month) with 72-hour notice. Emergency maintenance carveout limited to events that materially threaten user data or integrity.
- Exceptions: experimental features and any customer-configured beta models flagged in the order form are excluded from SLA coverage.

Attached: GF_SLA_Table_v1.xlsx (updated), proposed_orderform_snippet.txt (included inline below).

--- proposed_orderform_snippet.txt ---
Dedicated Capacity — Model Profile and Latency SLOs:
1. Customer shall specify a Model Profile in the Order Form which includes the model family, quantization configuration (if applicable), and the concurrency cap.
2. Redwood will provision Dedicated GPU capacity to support the Model Profile. Latency SLOs apply only when the Customer routes traffic that conforms to the Model Profile and does not exceed the concurrency cap.
3. Autoscaling and burst capacity are provided as optional add-ons and are not covered by the latency SLO unless explicitly added to the Order Form.

Credits and Measurement:
1. Availability is measured per rolling 30-day window. Service Credits are calculated as a percentage of the monthly fee as described in GF_SLA_Table_v1.xlsx.
2. Customer must report SLA incidents via the Redwood Console within 14 days to be eligible for credits.

--- end snippet ---
